name: Bloom
description: Reverb with evolving spectral tails: the tail is read through reversed, pitch-shifted grains and fed back into itself, so the shift grows the longer a sound has been ringing.

params.name: Bloom
params.description: How far the tail drifts in pitch as it rings, and how much of the shifted sound feeds back. At zero the pitch stays put.

params.name: Direction
params.description: Up drifts the tail higher and Down lower. Scatter sends some grains up and others down at the same time.

params.name: Season
params.description: Tone of the tail. Spring is the brightest, Summer is full, Autumn rolls off the highs and Winter is the darkest.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the tail rings. Longer settings also make the pitch drift arrive more slowly.

params.name: Seed
params.description: Subtle colouring of the tail. Fundamental leans on the lows, Odd adds a hollow edge and Even a rounder one.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the reverb. Fully up is the drifting tail alone.

params.name: Interval
params.description: The pitch the tail drifts towards: a fifth, an octave, or both at once. Atonal drifts smoothly with no fixed interval.

params.name: Width
params.description: Stereo width of the whole output, dry signal included. Zero is mono, the middle is normal stereo and the top is extra wide.

deviations: bloom, mix and width are 0..1 instead of 0..100 % (the source divides by 100; same laws and defaults)
decay: JUCE skew 0.4 becomes a log taper; range 1..30 s and default 5 s unchanged
LFO depth: 18 samples at any rate in the source; here 18 x rate / 44100 (0.408 ms at every rate; 19.6 samples at 48 kHz)

damping pole 0.45, DC-blocker pole 0.995 and the feedback-gain smoothing pole 0.999 are per-sample constants in the source; here each is raised to the power 44100 / rate, which keeps the 5.6 kHz damping corner, the 35 Hz DC corner and the 23 ms glide of 44.1 kHz at every rate (identical at 44.1 kHz; at 48 kHz the plugin's corners sit 8.8 % higher)

above 64 kHz the reverb core (diffusers, lines, age tracker, drifters) runs at half the host rate behind kit::Halfband2x (63-tap halfband down and up), because SpectralDrifter's grain length, ratio smoothing and second output low-pass are sample counts inside the shared class: 88.2/96 kHz behave as 44.1/48 kHz. Only the wet path is resampled (about 0.65 ms of extra pre-delay at 96 kHz); the dry path and the widener stay at the host rate. Above 128 kHz the core runs at 88.2/96 kHz and the drifter's sample-count constants are twice as fast, as they would be in the plugin
MAX_DELAY_SAMPLES 44100 (a one-second cap counted in samples) becomes 32768-sample lines: the longest line is 0.177 s, so no rate up to a 185 kHz core rate is clamped

the feedback-gain target is recomputed when decay changes instead of once per host block (the source reads the unsmoothed parameter per block); a decay set before the first block snaps instead of gliding from the 5 s default

juce::SmoothedValue 5 ms linear ramps on bloom, mix and width become kit::LinearRamp 5 ms; smoothedDecay, which the source advances but never reads, is dropped; parameter changes take effect at the sample they arrive on, not at the next host block
std::sin per line per sample becomes a coupled-form sine oscillator per line (same rates 0.1 + 0.025 i Hz, same golden-ratio start phases)
juce::ScopedNoDenormals becomes flush_denormal on the diffuser, interpolator, damping, DC-blocker and age states
the normalised age is clamped to 1 before it reaches the drifter (in the source it can exceed 1 for a moment after decay is lowered while a tail rings)

width: below 0.25 the side signal left by StereoWidener is faded to zero so that width 0 is exactly mono; the widener alone keeps the band under its 200 Hz crossover at full width when width is 0 (measured side 9 to 14 dB under mid on Bloom's tail). From 0.25 up the output is the source's
StereoWidener::setWidth is called only on samples where the ramped width changes (same output, no per-sample sqrt)
kit::IdleGate: once the network and the output have stayed under -140 dBFS for one second the device stops and returns exact zero; the plugin runs continuously
the UI meters (input and output peaks, currentDrift, decayProgress) and the JUCE state/program plumbing are not ported
the plugin has no presets: the seven presets are new, the first being the source's defaults

constants carried over unchanged: 8 lines of 4799..7789 samples and 4 diffusers of 142, 107, 379, 277 samples at 44.1 kHz, diffusion 0.75 / 0.625, damping 0.45, DC pole 0.995, drift injection 0.25, wet headroom 0.35 (rate handling as listed for PluginProcessor.cpp)
std::array members become kit::DelayLine and plain arrays in one static object; atomics for the editor dropped
reused unchanged from cpp/devices/spectral-drifter, whose manifest records its de-JUCE edits (jlimit to std::clamp, MathConstants to kPi, two test hooks)
reused unchanged from cpp/devices/spectral-drifter, whose manifest records its edits (MathConstants to kPi, flush_denormal on the eight one-pole states)

origin.note: bloom_reverb.h is Bloom's processBlock rebuilt on cpp/kit: the algorithm, its constants and its quirks are the plugin's (the four input diffusers are Schroeder allpasses without the (1 - k^2) term and therefore resonant combs; the wet path is the drifters' output only). SpectralDrifter and StereoWidener are the copies live-mix already builds for spectral-drifter, stereo-widener and felt-piano, compiled in through `sources`. PluginEditor.h/.cpp (the WebView UI) are not ported.
